skill.name: clinicaltrials-database
skill.description: Query ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 for trial searches, NCT ID lookups, status and phase filters, pagination, summaries, and CSV exports.
skill.summary: Search and summarize public ClinicalTrials.gov trial records through API v2.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are explainable by the skill purpose: public ClinicalTrials.gov API calls, documentation examples, and explicit CSV export snippets. I found no prompt injection, credential access, hidden command execution, arbitrary network destinations, or malicious persistence in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Network helper functions do not consistently set request timeouts.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit timeouts to all requests.get calls and document retry behavior for bulk queries.

remediation.issue: Bulk pagination can collect many records if users choose broad filters.
remediation.suggestion: Keep max_results or page limits visible in examples and recommend narrow filters for large searches.

content.value_statement: Clinical trial searches can be slow when users must assemble API parameters manually. This skill guides focused ClinicalTrials.gov queries, detail lookups, pagination, and export workflows.
actual_capabilities: Search public trials by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, NCT ID, and phase.
Retrieve detailed study records by NCT ID from ClinicalTrials.gov API v2.
Extract trial summaries with title, status, phase, enrollment, and update dates.
Guide pagination for large result sets and bulk retrieval planning.
Request JSON or CSV responses for analysis and reporting workflows.
limitations: It depends on the public ClinicalTrials.gov API and its availability, schema, and rate limits.
It does not verify whether a patient qualifies for a trial or replace clinical judgment.
It only returns data exposed by ClinicalTrials.gov and may include incomplete records.
Large searches may require pagination controls to avoid excessive API requests.

use_cases.title: Find Recruiting Options
use_cases.description: Search recruiting trials by condition, treatment, and location for an initial referral list.

use_cases.title: Track Drug Development
use_cases.description: Identify trials for a drug, sponsor, or phase to monitor research activity.

use_cases.title: Prepare Trial Datasets
use_cases.description: Collect trial records, summarize key fields, and export CSV data for review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Condition Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search ClinicalTrials.gov for recruiting trials for type 2 diabetes. Show NCT ID, title, status, phase, and location summary.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Trial Record
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up NCT04852770 and summarize its purpose, eligibility criteria, status, phase, sponsor, and listed contacts.

prompt_templates.title: Match by Patient Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a focused shortlist without giving medical advice.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find recruiting lung cancer immunotherapy trials in California. Prioritize Phase 2 or Phase 3 trials and include key eligibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Export Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a paginated ClinicalTrials.gov search for Alzheimer trials with results. Include filters, fields to extract, rate limit handling, and CSV columns.

output_examples.input: Find recruiting breast cancer trials near Boston.
output: A concise table of matching studies with NCT ID, trial title, current status, phase, facility city, and sponsor.
A short note that eligibility must be confirmed with the trial team or treating clinician.

output_examples.input: Summarize NCT04852770 for a research brief.
output_examples.output: A plain-language trial brief covering study purpose, phase, enrollment, intervention, eligibility highlights, sponsor, status, and last update date.

output_examples.input: Export completed Alzheimer studies with results.
output_examples.output: A CSV-oriented field plan with study identifiers, titles, completion status, result availability, sponsor names, enrollment counts, and update dates.

best_practices: Use specific conditions, interventions, locations, and statuses to keep result sets manageable.
Respect ClinicalTrials.gov rate limits when paginating or collecting large datasets.
Review eligibility criteria and contact details before using results for referral workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not treat trial search results as medical advice or final eligibility decisions.
Do not run broad unbounded searches when a targeted query can answer the question.
Do not assume every ClinicalTrials.gov record has complete contacts, locations, or results.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 is public and does not require authentication.

faq.question: Can it search by NCT ID?
faq.answer: Yes. It can retrieve a specific study record when you provide an NCT identifier.

faq.question: Can it help match patients to trials?
faq.answer: It can create research shortlists, but clinicians and trial teams must confirm eligibility.

faq.question: Can results be exported?
faq.answer: Yes. The referenced workflow supports JSON and CSV responses for analysis.

faq.question: What data source does it use?
faq.answer: It uses the public ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 maintained by the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

faq.question: Does it include historical trial results?
faq.answer: It can filter for completed studies and identify records with results when the API exposes them.
